topicDisplay: Paper 1 Exploring Modern And Literary Heritage Texts
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the assessment objectives.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does Dickens use the Cratchit family to highlight about Victorian society?
options: The dignity and hardship of the working poor
questions.explain: The loving but struggling Cratchits dramatise poverty and the case for social responsibility.

questions.q: What two emaciated children does the Ghost of Christmas Present reveal beneath his robe?
questions.explain: The children Ignorance and Want symbolise the dangers of neglecting the poor.

options: Two characters say the same line
The audience knows something a character does not
questions.explain: Dramatic irony arises from the gap between the audience's knowledge and a character's ignorance, creating tension or poignancy.

questions.q: At the start of A Christmas Carol, how is Scrooge described?
options: A cold, miserly and unfeeling man
questions.explain: Scrooge is "a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous old sinner".

questions.q: When the gentlemen ask Scrooge to give to the poor early on, what does he suggest they rely on instead?
questions.explain: Scrooge points to "the prisons" and "the workhouses", echoing harsh Victorian Poor Law attitudes.

questions.q: A 'soliloquy' in a play is best defined as...
options: A speech where a character alone on stage reveals their inner thoughts
A short comment to the audience while others are present
questions.explain: In a soliloquy the character is alone and voices private thoughts, letting the audience access their inner mind.

questions.q: What does Marley's ghost wear that symbolises a life devoted to greed?
options: A chain of cash-boxes, keys and ledgers
questions.explain: His chain is made of "cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers", the heavy weight of his earthly avarice.

questions.q: 'Pathetic fallacy' is a technique in which a writer...
options: Gives weather or nature human emotions to reflect mood
questions.explain: Pathetic fallacy projects human feelings onto the natural world or weather, often mirroring a character's emotional state.

questions.q: Who is the first spirit to visit Scrooge, warning him of his fate?
questions.explain: Marley, Scrooge's dead business partner, appears bound in chains he "forged in life".

questions.q: What is the name of the young woman whose death the Inspector investigates?
questions.explain: The dead girl is Eva Smith, who also went by the name Daisy Renton.

options: A stanza of exactly four lines
questions.explain: Blank verse is unrhymed lines of iambic pentameter, much used by Shakespeare for noble characters.
Iambic pentameter contains five iambs (da-DUM x5), giving roughly ten syllables and a rhythm close to natural speech.
